what_its_for: Cyclopentolate is an eye drop used to widen (dilate) your pupil and temporarily stop your eye from focusing. Your doctor uses it during eye exams to get a better look at the back of your eye, or before certain eye procedures. It is also sometimes used to treat inflammation inside the eye.
how_to_take: Wash your hands well before using. Tilt your head back, gently pull down your lower eyelid to make a small pocket, and place the prescribed number of drops into that pocket. Close your eye gently for 1 to 2 minutes — do not blink or squeeze your eye shut hard. Press lightly on the inner corner of your eye (near your nose) for about 1 to 2 minutes to keep the medicine from draining into your body. If you wear contact lenses, remove them before using the drops. Ask your doctor when you can put them back in.
dosing: Your doctor or eye care provider will tell you exactly how many drops to use and how often. Usually 1 to 2 drops are placed in the affected eye(s) once, about 40 to 50 minutes before your eye exam or procedure. Do not use more drops than prescribed. Always follow the instructions given to you at your appointment.
missed_dose: Cyclopentolate is usually given just once at a clinic visit, so a missed dose is unlikely. If you are using it at home on a schedule and miss a dose, use it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Never double up on doses.
storage: Store at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C and 25°C). Keep the bottle tightly closed when not in use. Keep away from heat, light, and moisture. Keep out of reach of children. Do not freeze. Throw away the drops after the expiration date on the label.
what_to_avoid: Your vision will be blurry and your eyes will be very sensitive to light for several hours after using cyclopentolate. Do NOT drive, operate heavy machinery, or do activities that need clear vision until your sight returns to normal. Wear sunglasses outdoors to protect your eyes from bright light. Avoid touching the tip of the eye drop bottle to your eye, fingers, or any surface to prevent contamination.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency care if you experience: severe eye pain or redness, sudden vision changes, fast or irregular heartbeat, feeling confused or very restless, difficulty urinating, skin that is flushed, hot, or very dry, a high fever, or signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, swelling of the face or throat, or trouble breathing. These may be signs of a serious reaction. In children, watch closely for unusual behavior, drowsiness, or rapid heartbeat after use.
when_it_works: Cyclopentolate starts working within about 15 to 30 minutes after the drops are placed in your eye. The full effect (widest pupil dilation) usually occurs within 30 to 60 minutes. The blurry vision and light sensitivity may last anywhere from a few hours to about 24 hours, and sometimes up to 2 days. Your vision should return to normal on its own without any treatment.
special_populations: Children: Cyclopentolate should be used with caution in infants and young children because they are more likely to have serious side effects such as rapid heart rate, fever, flushing, and behavioral changes. A lower concentration (0.5%) is usually used in infants. Parents should monitor their child closely for at least 30 minutes after use. Older Adults: Older adults, especially those with a history of glaucoma or high pressure in the eye, should use this medication with caution. It can raise eye pressure. Tell your doctor if you or a family member has glaucoma before this drop is used. Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or breastfeeding. This medication is generally used only when clearly needed during pregnancy. If breastfeeding, ask your doctor about timing feedings around the eye drops.
